text:
sarah_sales: Hey team — Petrichor Health wants a Private deployment POC next month. Requirements they listed: no internet egress from our infra, preserve client source IP for audit logs, only allowlist a small set of FQDNs, and TLS inspection sits in their DMZ. Two-week POC window. Any immediate blockers?

raj_network: Quick callouts: preserving client src IP across AWS PrivateLink is tricky — interface endpoints terminate at the ENI in our VPC, so origin IP is not preserved to the service container. Options: do VPC peering (src IP preserved) or run a NLB with proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For.

raj_network: If customer insists on PrivateLink for security reasons we can add a transparent proxy in their VPC (sidecar NLB -> proxy) to keep observable client IPs. Tradeoffs: extra ops and connection NATing. :thinking_face:

jordan_se: Pricing heads-up: PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint + data-processing fees. For expected 2M tokens/day during POC, raw egress bytes could push costs — recommend we model both PrivateLink and peering with egress through their NAT for cost parity. I can run a quick estimate if you share token -> byte assumptions.

maria_security: From security questionnaire perspective we need: network diagram, list of allowed CIDR blocks, endpoint architecture (PrivateLink vs peering), key management approach (customer KMS or ours), SOC2 cert copy, and cert rotation process. Also confirm whether customer will do TLS termination or we do inside the private deployment.

devon_sales: @maria_security they specifically said TLS inspection happens in their DMZ so they will terminate and re-encrypt to our service. They asked if we can expose an allowlist of hostnames instead of IPs.

raj_network: Hostname allowlist works if using egress FQDN filtering on their side, but PrivateLink uses interface IPs — so firewall rules might be IP-based. If they want FQDN-level allowlisting, they should put an outbound proxy that does SNI/FQDN allowlist and only permit traffic to our endpoint IPs. Example firewall snippet they can use:```
# allow outbound to Redwood private endpoint
allow tcp from 10.12.0.0/16 to 198.51.100.45/32 port 443
# if using proxy: allow proxy egress to redwood-hostnames
allow tcp from 10.12.10.0/24 to proxy.dmz.corp:3128
```

maria_security: Also add requirement for mutual TLS (mTLS) between their proxy and our service if they re-encrypt. We'll need cert exchange workflow.

jordan_se: For the POC timeline we should propose: week0 prep (network diagram + security Q finished), week1 infra + smoke tests, week2 load validation and handoff. Need their network team availability for the prep week.

devon_sales: I'll loop in their infra lead. @raj_network can you draft a short decision matrix (PrivateLink vs Peering vs NLB-proxy) with pros/cons and a recommended default for auditors? A one-pager we can attach to the SOW.

raj_network: Yep. I'll post the matrix here later today. Quick sketch: PrivateLink = strong isolation, simpler account boundaries, extra endpoint fees, src IP not preserved; VPC peering = src IP preserved, lower per-connection fees, broader network surface; NLB+proxy = preserves observability, adds ops & latency.

sarah_sales: Awesome. Also flagging licensing/pricing ask from procurement: can we provide a capped egress estimate for the POC period (billing cap)? Jordan — can you include that in the estimate?

jordan_se: Will do. I'll produce a conservative estimate + a capped quote option.

deploy-bot: [deployment] preflight check passed for private-deploy-poc (infra-checks: ok, certs: pending).

devon_sales: Thanks everyone — next steps: raj to upload decision matrix, jordan to send pricing + cap options, maria to share required security artifacts checklist. I'll book an intro with the customer's network lead for Tue. :thumbsup:
